==English==
{{wp}}

===Alternative forms===
* {{alt|en|traffick|qq1=archaic|traffique|qq2=obsolete}}

===Etymology===
From {{bor|en|frm|trafique}}, {{m|frm|traffique||traffic}}, from {{der|en|it|traffico||traffic}} from {{m|it|trafficare||to carry on trade}}. Potentially from {{der|en|la-vul|*trānsfrīcāre||to rub across}}; Klein instead suggests the Italian has ultimate origin in {{der|en|ar|تَفْرِيق||distribution, dispersion}}, reshaped to match the native prefix {{m|it|tra-||trans-}}.
{{root|en|ar|ف ر ق}}<!--possibly--> Displaced native {{noncog|ang|mangung||traffic, trade, commerce}}.

The adjectival sense is possibly influenced by {{der|en|tl|trapik}} and follows a general trend in Philippine English to construct a noun from an adjective.<ref>{{R:OED Online|entry=traffic|pos=adj|id=33840333|date=December 2021}}</ref>

===Pronunciation===
* {{enPR|trăf'ĭk}}, {{IPA|en|/ˈtɹæfɪk/|a=RP,GA}}
* {{audio|en|En-us-traffic.ogg|a=GA}}
* {{rhymes|en|æfɪk|s=2}}
* {{hyphenation|en|traf|fic}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun|-|s}}

# {{senseid|en|movement}} Moving [[pedestrian]]s or [[vehicle]]s, or the [[flux]] or [[passage]] thereof.
#: {{syn|en|[[travel]] (U.S.)}}
#: {{ux|en|The '''traffic''' is slow during [[rush hour]].}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Romeo and Juliet Q1-2|chapter=Prologue|passage=VVhoſe miſaduentures, piteous ouerthrovves, / (Through the continuing of their Fathers ſtrife, / And death-markt paſſage of their Parents rage) / Is novv the tvvo hovvres '''traffique''' of our Stage.}}
# {{senseid|en|commercial}} The [[commercial]] [[transportation]] or [[exchange]] of [[goods]], or the movement of [[passenger]]s or people.
#* {{RQ:Defoe Crusoe|passage=I had three large axes, and abundance of hatchets (for we carried the hatchets for '''traffic''' with the Indians).}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2007|author=John Darwin|title=After Tamerlane|publisher=Penguin|page=12
|passage=Its units of study are regions or oceans, long-distance trades [...], the '''traffic''' of cults and beliefs between cultures and continents.}}
# A flow of [[customer]]s for a [[store]] or [[restaurant]].
#: {{ux|en|Sales are down due to a decline in store '''traffic'''.}}
# {{senseid|en|illegal}} The [[illegal]] [[trade]] or [[exchange]] of [[goods]], often [[drug]]s.
#: {{syn|en|trafficking<q:more common>}}
#* {{RQ:Guardian|author=Alfred W. McCoy|title=How the heroin trade explains the US-UK failure in Afghanistan|date=2018-01-09|url=https://www.theguardian.com/news/2018/jan/09/how-the-heroin-trade-explains-the-us-uk-failure-in-afghanistan|passage=They, in turn, had long dominated the drug '''traffic''' in the area of north-east Afghanistan that they controlled during the Taliban years.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261022095104/https://www.theguardian.com/news/2018/jan/09/how-the-heroin-trade-explains-the-us-uk-failure-in-afghanistan|archivedate=22 October 2026}}
# {{senseid|en|exchange}} The exchange or [[flux]] of [[information]], [[message]]s or [[data]], as in a computer or telephone [[network]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1902|author=John Buchan|title=The Outgoing of the Tide
|passage=The parish stank of idolatry, abominable rites were practiced in secret, and in all the bounds there was no one had a more evil name for the black '''traffic''' than one Alison Sempill, who bode at the Skerburnfoot.}}
#* {{RQ:Guardian|author=Charles Arthur|title=Porn sites get more internet traffic in UK than social networks or shopping|date=2013-07-26|url=https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2013/jul/26/porn-sites-internet-traffic-uk|passage=Internet '''traffic''' to legal pornography sites in the UK comprised 8.5% of all "clicks" on web pages in June – exceeding those for shopping, news, business or social networks, according to new data obtained exclusively by the Guardian.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261016230022/https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2013/jul/26/porn-sites-internet-traffic-uk|archivedate=16 October 2026}}
## {{lb|en|radio}} Of [[CB radio]], formal written messages relayed on behalf of others.
## {{lb|en|advertising}} The amount of attention paid to a particular printed page etc., in a publication.
# {{senseid|en|commodities}} The [[commodity|commodities]] of the [[market]].
#* {{RQ:John Gay Trivia|passage=You'll see a draggled damsel / From Billingsgate her fishy '''traffic''' bear.}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb|~s|~king|~ked}}

# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To pass goods and [[commodity|commodities]] from one person to another for an equivalent in goods or money; to buy or sell goods.
#: {{syn|en|trade#Verb}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To trade [[meanly]] or [[mercenarily]]; to [[bargain#Verb|bargain]].
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To exchange in traffic; to effect by a bargain or for a [[consideration]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1912|title=The World's Wit and Humor|page=176
|passage=A Libyan longing took us, and we would have chosen, if we could, to bear a strand of grotesque beads, or a handful of brazen gauds, and '''traffic''' them for some sable maid with crisp locks, whom, uncoffling from the captive train beside the desert, we should make to do our general housework forever, through the right of lawful purchase.}}
